about: Zenkai Rules Z1 intent examples: card t_90e75c20, the run-level disk guard. gauntlet.runner.Runner refuses to start the next case and parks the rest of the layer, reason 'disk', once free disk (decimal GB, as `df -H` reports) is below DISK_MIN_GB (25.0) -- the same shape as the existing usage-meter parker (Park raised before any session work for the case begins, no case result written for it). The free-space reading is injected through the Runner's own `free_disk_gb` parameter (never by mocking shutil.disk_usage, the subject). Run by tests/intent/test_disk_guard_intent.py, a real tiny run of the engine (gauntlet.runner.Runner) over the toy adapter (gauntlet.tests.toy) in a temp dir -- no darktable, no real gauntlet run. Two oracles per example: the run's own status, and whether the first case in the layer got a written result at all -- a guard that parks the run but still lets a case sneak a result through is as wrong as one that never triggers.
subject: gauntlet/runner.py:Runner (the disk guard added in _run_layer)

examples.source: card t_90e75c20: incident 2026-09-28 13:58, disk filled at 21/40 cases -- the guard must refuse before a case even starts, not after ENOSPC
'below 25 GB' is a strict less-than; the boundary itself must never park
the common case: the guard must stay silent when disk is not actually tight
